record.content_text:
The table in the previous section listed the names of large numbers made up of groups of ten. This table shows how to write numbers as powers of ten.

$$
\begin{array}{|l|l|l|}
  \hline
    \textbf{Name} & \textbf{Number} & \textbf{Powers of ten}  \\
    \hline
     \text{Ten} & 10 & 10=10^1    \\
    \hline
     \text{Hundred} & 100 & 10\times10=10^2    \\
    \hline
    \text{Thousand} & 1,000 & 10\times10\times10=10^3    \\
    \hline
    \text{Ten thousand} & 10,000 & 10\times10\times10\times10=10^4    \\
    \hline
    \text{Hundred thousand} & 100,000 & 10\times10\times10\times10\times10=10^5    \\
    \hline
    \text{Million} & 1,000,000 & 10\times10\times10\times10\times10\times10=10^6    \\
    \hline
    \text{Ten million} & 10,000,000 & 10\times10\times10\times10\times10\times10\times10=10^7 \\
    \hline
    \text{Hundred million} & 100,000,000 & 10\times10\times10\times10\times10\times10\times10\times10=10^8 \\
    \hline
    \text{Billion} & 1,000,000,000 & 10\times10\times10\times10\times10\times10\times10\times10\times10=10^9 \\
    \hline
     \end{array}
$$

The number 1,000,000,000 is named one billion. Try to imagine how large one billion is:

- One billion seconds from your birth, you will be just over 31 years and 8 months old.
- One billion sheets of photocopy paper stacked on top of each other would reach almost 110 km into the sky.

We may count from zero to ten million in millions:
0: zero
1,000,000: one million
2,000,000: two million
3,000,000: three million
4,000,000: four million
5,000,000: five million
6,000,000: six million
7,000,000: seven million
8,000,000: eight million
9,000,000: nine million
10,000,000: ten million

This counting chart may be used to count to 1,000,000,000 in ten millions and in hundred millions.

![](https://electricbookworks.github.io/siyavula-open-textbooks-images/items/images/web/ebw-jss1-01-007.png)

record.answer_text:

3.5 million = 3,500,000: three million five hundred thousand
4.5 million = 4,500,000: four million five hundred thousand

record.answer_text:

closest_candidate_atomic_objectives.proposed_objective_text: Count to one million in specified place-value increments.
closest_candidate_atomic_objectives.evidence_quote: Use the following counting chart to count to 1,000,000 in ten thousands and in hundred thousands.
closest_candidate_atomic_objectives.rationale: The records teach counting up to one million in hundred-thousands, ten-thousands, thousands, hundreds, tens, and units. That is prerequisite evidence for million-scale counting but not the same as the canonical AO 'Count in millions.'

closest_candidate_atomic_objectives.proposed_objective_text: Count with large numbers by specified place-value increments.
closest_candidate_atomic_objectives.evidence_quote: If you count in thousands, the digit in the "**th**" column must increase.
closest_candidate_atomic_objectives.rationale: These records teach a broader counting-by-place-value procedure inside large numbers. One exercise that counts directly in millions is linked to the existing AO; the remaining hundred-thousand and hundred increment records are adjacent enrichment rather than direct AO evidence.
